title: Measuring the Excess Owed on a ShieldCare Claim
content:
The excess owed on a Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plan is measured from the plan's own history of
excesses billed and excess payments received, and from the standing of the plan.

| What the records show | How the excess owed is measured |
| --- | --- |
| the excesses billed on the plan come to more than what stands settled against them, no excess payment stands on the plan inside the last 12 months, and the plan stands active | the excess owed is every excess standing unsettled on the plan, the excesses billed less the excess payments received |
| the excesses billed come to more than what stands settled against them, and an excess payment stands on the plan inside the last 12 months | the excess owed is the excess most recently billed on the plan alone |
| every other plan | the excess owed is the plan's deductible |

### Points of judgement

All three limbs of the first row must hold together: an excess payment anywhere inside the last 12
months moves the measure to the second row, and a plan that does not stand active moves it out of the
first row altogether. Where the excesses billed come to no more than what stands settled against them,
neither of the first two rows is reached and the excess owed is the plan's own deductible figure.

### A case on hypothetical figures

A plan with nothing billed against it at all takes the plan's deductible as the excess owed. Take instead a plan
standing active whose excesses billed come to 144.00 — one of 99.00 and, later, one of 45.00 — against 45.00
received. Where an excess payment stands inside the last 12 months, the excess owed is the most recently billed
excess alone, 45.00. Where no excess payment stands inside that time, the excess owed is every excess standing
unsettled, the 144.00 billed less the 45.00 received, that is 99.00.
